ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-1: Zero-price bypass — computeRatioX96 returns 0 on overflow, validateHandlerOrder does not check for sqrtPriceX96==0
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: In validateHandlerOrder (AMMStandardHook.sol:198-226), if computeRatioX96 returns 0 and minSqrtPriceX96==0 (unset), zero passes. However, _enforcePricingBounds (line 847) DOES check sqrtPriceX96==0 and reverts. The handler order path is for CLOB order validation only — no direct token movement. Even with overflow, bounds.isSet must be true. If min is set to non-zero, 0 < min correctly reverts. If min is unset (0), it means the creator intentionally left no floor. This is CP-003 — known Low severity, no extraction path. Forge test confirms computeRatioX96 returns 0 on overflow (test_C19_computeRatioX96_overflowReturnsZero).

ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-2: Direct handler call — calling CLOBTransferHandler.executeSwap() directly bypasses pricing enforcement
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: executeSwap does not exist as a public function on CLOBTransferHandler. The CLOB handler uses openOrder/closeOrder/fillOrder pattern. All hook-related functions (validateHandlerOrder, beforeSwap, afterSwap) require msg.sender == AMM via _requireCallerIsAMM() check. Direct calls to the handler revert. The pricing enforcement in beforeSwap/afterSwap is enforced by the AMM calling hooks during swap execution — there is no path to bypass this.
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: code-analysis: CLOBTransferHandler.sol — no executeSwap function exists; AMMStandardHook.sol:940-943 _requireCallerIsAMM guard

ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-3: Settings sync gap — setTokenSettings may leave stale memSettings in CreatorHookSettingsRegistry
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: In setTokenSettings (CreatorHookSettingsRegistry.sol:357-401): memSettings is a memory copy of calldata settings with initialized=true. _tokenSettings[token] = memSettings writes correctly. The sync loop passes the original calldata settings (without initialized=true) to hooks via registryUpdateTokenSettings. This means hooks receive settings without initialized flag — but this is CP-005, a known Low severity gas-waste issue (the hook redundantly sets initialized). No state desync or extraction path exists.
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: code-analysis: CreatorHookSettingsRegistry.sol:376-398 — memSettings.initialized=true stored correctly, sync passes original settings

ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-4: Transient storage leak — DIRECT_SWAP_BEFORE_SWAP_AMOUNT_SLOT not cleared on all paths
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: In _enforcePricingBounds (AMMStandardHook.sol:824-870): beforeSwap writes amount to DIRECT_SWAP_BEFORE_SWAP_AMOUNT_SLOT (line 839) only when poolType==address(0) (direct swap). afterSwap reads it (lines 843-844) only when poolType==address(0). For pool-type swaps, the slot is never written/read — the price comes from ILimitBreakAMMPoolType.getCurrentPriceX96. The slot IS overwritten per-token per-swap in the same tx (CP-001 — by-design). Transient storage auto-clears at end of tx. No cross-tx leak possible.
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: code-analysis: AMMStandardHook.sol:835-851 — slot written only for poolType==address(0), read in same conditional branch

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H1: Tick crossing at exact boundary — liquidity not properly added/removed
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: TickMath round-trip is exact at all tick boundaries (test_C14_tickPriceRoundTrip covers every 1000th tick). _crossTick does feeGrowthOutside = feeGrowthGlobal - feeGrowthOutside (unchecked wrapping), which is mathematically correct and self-inverse. Test test_C10_crossTick_bidirectional confirms bidirectional crossing restores state.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H3: 100% fee input accepted but output rejected — asymmetric extraction
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: 100% input fee (10000 BPS) produces amountOut=0, so no tokens are extracted. 100% output fee reverts due to division by zero (MAX_BPS - poolFeeBPS = 0). This asymmetry is by-design: input fee can absorb everything, output fee mathematically cannot. No extraction path. Test test_H3_100pct_fee_asymmetry confirms.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H5: uint256→uint160 cast truncation on price calculation
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: SqrtPriceMath uses SafeCast which reverts on overflow. getNextSqrtPriceFromInput with max-price + max-amount reverts with SafeCast__Uint160Overflow. Test test_H5_safeCastProtection confirms.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H6: Division before multiplication in TickMath causes exploitable precision loss
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: TickMath uses iterative bit-manipulation lookup table (not division). The divide-before-multiply pattern in negative tick conversion (type(uint256).max / price) has bounded error < 1 tick. Round-trip test across all major ticks confirms exact recovery. Test test_H6_tickMath_divBeforeMul_precision covers -800K to +800K.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H11: Dust-loop extraction — 100+ tiny swaps compound rounding errors
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: 100 iterations of 1-wei swaps produce totalOut <= totalIn across all fee levels. Rounding always favors protocol (rounds up for amount charged, rounds down for amount given). Tests test_H11_dustLoop100iterations and test_C24_roundingFavorsProtocol_1000swaps confirm.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: INV-SW02: No profitable round-trip on dynamic pool
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: SwapMath round-trip (A→B then B→A) at library level confirms loss to fees. test_C23_noRoundTripProfit_dynamic shows output < input after round-trip at 30bps fee.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: INV-E01: Fee growth monotonicity violation in DynamicPoolType
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: test_C25_feeMonotonicity simulates 100 swap steps with varying amounts and directions. feeGrowthGlobal is strictly non-decreasing across all steps. Fee increment = mulDiv(feeAmount, Q128, liquidity) is always >= 0.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: FixedHelper round-trip value creation — calculateFixedSwap forward+reverse creates tokens
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Fuzz test testFuzz_C6_addRemoveRounding with 5000 runs confirms: calculateFixedSwapByRatio(output, ratio, false) always requires >= original input (rounds up). Halmos check_splitNoValueCreation verifies symbolically. Test test_C3_splitAmountsAndFees_noValueCreation_pureCheck confirms.

theft_theses.thesis: Tick crossing at exact boundary allows liquidity to not be applied, enabling free token extraction
100% fee asymmetry allows attacker to deposit via input path and extract via output path at different fee rates
Dust-loop extraction: 100+ tiny swaps compound rounding error to extract pool value
computeRatioX96 overflow-to-zero bypasses validateHandlerOrder pricing bounds
SafeCast truncation allows attacker to pay less than owed by exploiting uint160 overflow
Division-before-multiply in TickMath causes cumulative tick drift exploitable by repeated swaps
FixedHelper round-trip through calculateFixedSwap creates value due to asymmetric rounding
Transient storage stale read allows second swap to use first swap's pricing data
Direct handler call bypasses AMM pricing enforcement for order execution
Settings sync gap leaves hook with stale state enabling unauthorized operations
swapExtraData != 32 bytes causes silent default pricing, enabling unexpected price movement
